correctness.rationale: All thresholds lie in a compact cube, every BSC outcome has positive probability for contrast below one, and exact cell/Walsh risk identities prove existence. The uniform even-power expansion yields a quadratic midpoint penalty and a linear pair-separation benefit. The fourth-order coefficient is directly reconstructed from Walsh orthogonality and first/second moments; its only first-order near-cluster change is +one quarter the sum of pair distances. A Lipschitz sixth-order remainder and a trial midpoint design force every global optimizer into an O(contrast^2) window. The sorted rescaled objective completes the square uniquely, giving the universal staircase and exact gain coefficient. The embedded exact-rational verifier passed 40 supplemental inequalities; finite cases do not replace the arbitrary-fixed-k proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-budget parallel localization under nearly useless binary measurements is a motivated stochastic-design problem. The result shows that naive exact replication at the midpoint is never asymptotically optimal for any fixed k>=3, derives the first nonzero global risk benefit and the universal arithmetic-progression geometry, and separates a vanishing reliability limit from long-code asymptotics. This is an exact general-k structural coefficient, not a numerical table or a routine addition of one query. Benefits vanish at sixth order and no claim about adaptive or finite-noise global uniqueness is made.
